## 1. The 3 official rubrics 2026 (summary)

### 1.1 TDP (Technical Description Paper) — maximum 102 pts

**Document:** [`Line&Maze_TDP_Rubrics_RCJ_Rescue_2026.pdf`](https://rescue.rcj.cloud/rules/2026/Line&Maze_TDP_Rubrics_RCJ_Rescue_2026.pdf) · [Template](https://rescue.rcj.cloud/rules/2026/TDP_Template_Line_Maze.docx)

Each **Key Element** is scored 0, 1-2, 3-4, or **5-6 (excellent)**. Total = 17 elements × 6 = 102 pts.

| Section | Key Elements | Max section |
|---|---|---|
| **Project Planning – from Design to Deployment** | Requirements definition · Overall Project Plan · Integration Plan / System Engineering | 18 |
| **Mechanical design and manufacturing** | Mechanical design structure and diagrams · Sub-module design and workability · Maker and/or innovative solutions · Reliability Tests and quality assurance | 24 |
| **Electronic design and manufacturing** | Electronic design structure and diagrams · Sub-module design and workability · Maker and/or innovative solutions · Reliability Tests and quality assurance | 24 |
| **Software** | Architecture design with diagrams (flowchart, UML, pseudocode) · Innovative solutions · Reliability Tests and quality assurance | 18 |
| **Performance Evaluation (competition challenges)** | Reliability Testing and Quality Assurance | 6 |
| **Document** | Contents, Conciseness and Clarity · Formatting | 12 |

**What separates 5-6 points from 3-4:** "**innovative**" and "**clearly identifies**" in each criterion. It is not enough to explain — you must show **diagrams, pseudocode, test results, integration paths**.

**New in 2026 (vs 2025):** all criteria now explicitly include "**Reliability Tests and quality assurance**." If coming from a 2025 TDP, that section needs to be created anew.

### 1.2 Poster — maximum 18 pts

**Document:** [`Line&Maze_Poster_Rubrics_RCJ_Rescue_2026.pdf`](https://rescue.rcj.cloud/rules/2026/Line&Maze_Poster_Rubrics_RCJ_Rescue_2026.pdf)

| Key Element | 0 | 1-2 | 3-4 | **5-6** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Team** | N/A | Name, league, country, members with generic role | + photos of members + specific roles | + **notable results and awards** + photos of the team in national competitions |
| **Hardware Line** | N/A | Photo of the robot + list of sensors and motors WITHOUT description | + description of each sensor with the associated task | + **highlighted innovative hardware solutions** with own image/sketch + explanation |
| **Software Line** | N/A | Only language + confusing attempt at explanation | + understandable flowchart of the main loop | + **relevant algorithms and methods** explained with pseudocode / flowchart / **test results** (outputs, graphs) |

**Specific suggestions from the committee for "innovative":**
- **Hardware Line:** custom chassis, victim capture mechanism, any innovative solution.
- **Software Line:** evacuation zone strategy, victim detection, line following, any innovative algorithm.

### 1.3 Video (Presentation Video) — maximum 24 pts

**Document:** [`Presentation_Video_Rubrics_RCJ_Rescue_2026.pdf`](https://rescue.rcj.cloud/rules/2026/Presentation_Video_Rubrics_RCJ_Rescue_2026.pdf) · [Guideline](https://rescue.rcj.cloud/rules/2026/Presentation_Video_Guideline_RCJ_Rescue_2026.pdf)

**General restrictions:**
- **Duration:** 5-7 min (beyond 7 min, only the first 7 are evaluated).
- **Language:** **English** mandatory. English subtitles optional or in the original language.
- **Format:** `.mp4`, maximum 500 MB.
- **Use:** projected at the international competition + possibly on the official RoboCup website.

| Section | Suggested time | 5-6 (excellent) |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Team Introduction** | 1 min 30 s | Clearly presents the team with photos. How it formed, first steps, roles, what inspired them. |
| **2. Robot Introduction** | 1 min | Presents the robot **using it on camera** to show hardware, innovations, and class diagram of the software. |
| **3. Robot In Action** | 2 min 15 s | Robot in action **while the team explains what it does**, not just footage. |
| **4. Future Plans** | 0 min 45 s | Clear future plan with concrete goals in RoboCup. |

**What separates 5-6 points from 3-4:** **showing the robot DOING**, not just describing. The team appears or is heard explaining while the robot executes.

## 3. TOPICS TO ANALYZE — TDP

> For each criterion of the TDP, what we have / what is missing / what to do / how much it costs / how much is gained.

### 3.1 Project Planning (max 18 pts)

#### TOPIC T1 — Requirements definition (max 6 pts)

**What we observe.** There is no document listing the requirements of the robot derived from the RCJ 2026 rules (e.g. "robot ≤ 250×250 mm", "must pass seesaw < 20°", "victims: 8 black + 4 silver + 2 false").

**What is missing.** A chapter of the TDP with: a numbered list of requirements, justification for each against the RCJ 2026 rules, hardware constraints of the team.

**Risk of NOT changing.** High — without this, maximum 1-2 pts in this criterion (4 pts lost).

**Risk of changing.** Low — it is writing, does not touch code.

**Estimated time.** 2 h (reading rules + writing + review between the two).

**Question for the team.** Do you have the 2026 edition of the rules ready? If not, first download the rules and read them as a group (1 h) before drafting requirements.

#### TOPIC T2 — Overall Project Plan (max 6 pts)

**What we observe.** There is no formal calendar, milestones by member, or review gates. The issue tracker has tasks but there is no consolidated roadmap.

**What is missing.** Table with: Sprint / Milestone / Owner / Target date / Status. Minimum 4-6 major milestones (e.g. "M1: stable line January", "M2: rescue zone February", "M3: tuning March", "M4: final TDP May", "M5: video + poster June").

**Risk of NOT changing.** High — automatically 1-2 pts in this criterion. Reflects management weakness.

**Risk of changing.** Low — writing + reconstructing the history.

**Estimated time.** 1.5 h (interview with Laureano/Benjamin about when each thing was done + writing).

**Question for the team.** Who has historical memory of the dates?

#### TOPIC T3 — Integration Plan / System Engineering (max 6 pts)

**What we observe.** The Mermaid diagram in `analisis-arquitectura-robotica.md` is a good starting point. It lacks how they connect, what comm protocols, what requirements each sub-component covers.

**What is missing.** Formal diagram (not just Mermaid) + table "component → what requirement it covers → how it connects to others".

**Risk of NOT changing.** Medium — the Mermaid only gives 3-4 pts. For 5-6 it needs to be formalized.

**Risk of changing.** Low — writing.

**Estimated time.** 2 h.

**Question for the team.** Do we use the existing Mermaid or redraw it in draw.io / Figma to make it look neater?

### 3.2 Mechanical design (max 24 pts)

#### TOPIC T4 — Mechanical design structure & diagrams (max 6 pts)

**What we observe.** STLs in `hardware/mechanical/_legacy/CAD/STLS/` + images of the robot in `_legacy/CAD/Imagenes/`. There is NO document explaining the design.

**What is missing.** Chapter with: orthogonal images (front, top, side), explanation of each major part (chassis, claw, motor mounts), why it was chosen (e.g. "4WD chassis for traction on a 25° ramp").

**Risk of NOT changing.** Medium-High — without this, maximum 1-2 pts.

**Risk of changing.** Low.

**Estimated time.** 2.5 h (Benjamin + Enzo, requires new photos or existing ones in the legacy).

#### TOPIC T5 — Mechanical sub-modules (max 6 pts)

Similar to T4 but focused on sub-modules: claw (5 servos), drivetrain, sensor mounts. Time: 1.5 h.

#### TOPIC T6 — Mechanical innovative solutions (max 6 pts)

**What we observe.** The robot **probably has innovations** (claw with 5 servos, sortLeft/sortRight, depositCenter — that is non-trivial). But they are not documented as such.

**What is missing.** Section "Mechanical Innovations" listing 1-3 things that the team designed originally (vs. kit parts). With photo + sketch + explanation of competitive advantage.

**Risk of NOT changing.** Medium — 3-4 pts maximum if not highlighted as innovative.

**Risk of changing.** Low.

**Estimated time.** 1 h.

**Question for the team.** What is our most original "mechanical feature"?

#### TOPIC T7 — Mechanical reliability tests (max 6 pts) ⚠️

**What we observe.** **Folder `testing/` is empty (`.gitkeep` only)**. There are no logs of systematic tests, nor evidence of QA.

**What is missing.** Documented tests: e.g. "10 runs of rescue zone, 8/10 successful, failures: ...". Ideally with table and graph.

**Risk of NOT changing.** **VERY HIGH** — automatically 0 pts in this criterion. And this pattern repeats in 4 of 5 sections of the TDP → ~24 pts lost in total.

**Risk of changing.** Low (it is documenting tests that have already been done informally) — but requires new discipline (noting future tests in `testing/TEST_LOG.md`).

**Estimated time.** 4 initial hours (reconstructing historical tests + creating template) + ~30 min/week ongoing.

**Question for the team.** Do you have a record of how many tests you ran? Videos? WhatsApp with results? Even if it is reconstructing 5-10 recent tests.

> **This is the TOPIC with the greatest impact from the analysis** — fix only this and we gain ~24 pts.

## 8. Technical fidelity verification (does the doc correspond with reality?)

Cross-check between the existing `docs/es/` and the current code of the repo:

| Doc states… | Code says… | Does it match? |
|---|---|---|
| "Non-blocking rescue FSM" (analisis-integral-ingenieria) | `actualizarRescate()` in `main.cpp:126-254` IS FSM | ✅ |
| "String comparison by pointer (P1 bug)" (various docs) | `drivebase.cpp:68` uses `strcmp(...)` correctly | ❌ Doc outdated — fixed |
| "Encoders without volatile" | `drivebase.h:24` has `volatile long pulseCount;` | ❌ Doc outdated — fixed |
| "YOLO model loads every time in rescue" | `Main.py:121-145` loads ONCE with warmup | ❌ Doc outdated — fixed |
| "Blocking delay() in claw" | `main.cpp:164,225,939-940,976-978,1152` still present | ✅ Doc current |
| "No serial heartbeat" | confirmed in main.cpp | ✅ Doc current |

**Conclusion.** There are **outdated docs** that state certain P0/P1 bugs still exist when they have already been fixed. Risk: if the team blindly copies to the TDP, they will be wrong due to contradictions with the actual code.

**Recommendation.** Before assembling the TDP, **review each technical analysis against the current code** and remove obsolete statements. Estimated time: 2 h (Enzo or the coach).

## 11. Final recommendation

**My honest recommendation:** that Lucio, Laureano, Benjamin, and Enzo sit down **for an entire afternoon** to execute the complete Phase 1 (download the template, create skeleton TDP file, start TEST_LOG, first pass of diagrams). That alone takes the team from ~10% of the score to ~22% in 6-7 hours — the steepest return curve of the entire campaign.

After that, distribute Phase 2 among the 4 with weekly deadlines and cross-review. Coach does the final pass.
